In Acre, the newly elected mesa marked a change from the preceding administration; in Amazonas, cooperation between ARENA and MDB under Governor Areosa contrasted with the more divisive approach of his predecessor. The material concerns state political institutions, party organization, legislative leadership, and relations between governing and opposition forces during the military regime established after the 1964 coup, when Brazil’s party system operated under authoritarian constraints.
